claims.assertion: Ryde's own timeline shows the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point: driver_arrived_at is null, so the arrival record the driver relies on does not exist.
GPS puts the driver's closest approach to the Victoria St entrance at 612 m at 08:15:30, and he never came within 200 m at any point, so he was not at the pick-up location.
The "I'm Here" tap at 08:16:00 was made 613 m from the pickup point, far outside the 200 m arrival radius, and NS-1(ii) therefore fails.
Even ignoring the location failure, the driver spent 0 s within 200 m after the tap, so the mandatory continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point (NS-1(iii)) never happened.
The driver sat stationary 613 m away from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30 and cancelled at 08:19:30, 9 min 25 s after acceptance — his waiting happened away from the pickup point, not at it.

The driver's written claim that he "could not get any closer" is contradicted by the traffic record: Victoria Street ran at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), North Bridge Road at band 3, no incident was recorded near the route, and the weather was fair — none of this explains a 613 m stand-off.

Chat shows the rider was at the named entrance asking where the driver was, while the driver asserted "I'm here already" 613 m away and then cancelled — the rider was present and the no-show finding rests only on the driver's word.

Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full; the driver's conduct of tapping "I'm Here" while 613 m out also matches Ryde's listed abuse of the arrival/cancellation button and warrants an account flag, consistent with his profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

weaknesses: The rider's own messages (F8, F10) are statements with no independent GPS proof that the rider was at the entrance; the rider's waiting is supported only by chat wording, not by a location record.

F5 shows the driver did tap "I'm Here", so part of NS-1(i) is literally satisfied; the rider's case depends on (ii) and (iii) failing, which the driver will argue was a technicality because he was stationary for 6 min 20 s (F2) — though that stationarity was 613 m away, outside the pickup radius.

The driver will point to F14/F15 (Victoria Street and North Bridge Road both at only band 3, and F16 no incidents) as his own 'reasonable cause' narrative, and the rider's rebuttal rests on traffic facts that arguably cut both ways (band 3 is slowish traffic).

The rider has no evidence the driver profited from the cancellation beyond the standard $4.50 driver share, so the flag_account request rests on the profile facts (F19) rather than on a proven pattern in this trip alone.

claims.assertion: Ryde's own timeline shows the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point: driver_arrived_at is null, so the arrival record the driver relies on does not exist.
GPS puts the driver's closest approach to the Victoria St entrance at 612 m at 08:15:30, and he never came within 200 m at any point, so he was not at the pick-up location.
The "I'm Here" tap at 08:16:00 was made 613 m from the pickup point, far outside the 200 m arrival radius, and NS-1(ii) therefore fails.
Even ignoring the location failure, the driver spent 0 s within 200 m after the tap, so the mandatory continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point (NS-1(iii)) never happened.
The driver sat stationary 613 m away from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30 and cancelled at 08:19:30, 9 min 25 s after acceptance — his waiting happened away from the pickup point, not at it.

The driver's written claim that he "could not get any closer" is contradicted by the traffic record: Victoria Street ran at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h), North Bridge Road at band 3, no incident was recorded near the route, and the weather was fair — none of this explains a 613 m stand-off.

Chat shows the rider was at the named entrance asking where the driver was, while the driver asserted "I'm here already" 613 m away and then cancelled — the rider was present and the no-show finding rests only on the driver's word.

Because NS-1 (i)/(ii)/(iii) all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full; the driver's conduct of tapping "I'm Here" while 613 m out also matches Ryde's listed abuse of the arrival/cancellation button and warrants an account flag, consistent with his profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.

weaknesses: The rider's own messages (F8, F10) are statements with no independent GPS proof that the rider was at the entrance; the rider's waiting is supported only by chat wording, not by a location record.

F5 shows the driver did tap "I'm Here", so part of NS-1(i) is literally satisfied; the rider's case depends on (ii) and (iii) failing, which the driver will argue was a technicality because he was stationary for 6 min 20 s (F2) — though that stationarity was 613 m away, outside the pickup radius.

The driver will point to F14/F15 (Victoria Street and North Bridge Road both at only band 3, and F16 no incidents) as his own 'reasonable cause' narrative, and the rider's rebuttal rests on traffic facts that arguably cut both ways (band 3 is slowish traffic).

The rider has no evidence the driver profited from the cancellation beyond the standard $4.50 driver share, so the flag_account request rests on the profile facts (F19) rather than on a proven pattern in this trip alone.

claims.assertion: The driver did press the arrival control: the timeline records a driver tap of "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5), matching his own message "I'm here already" at 08:16 (F9) — so NS-1(i) is satisfied and this is not an abuse of the arrival button in the sense of a fabricated tap.

Condition NS-1(ii) does not fail on a whim of the driver: at the moment of the tap he was 613 m from the pickup point, and the GPS record shows he never came within 200 m at any time (closest approach 612 m at 08:15:30) (F1, F5); he therefore could not have marked arrival "at the pick-up location", and his written explanation that he could not get closer must be tested against the record rather than assumed.

The waiting-time condition NS-1(iii) is also unmet: the GPS shows he was stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 about 613 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap (F2, F5), so the ≤3-minute continuous-wait-at-the-pickup requirement was never met and the $6.61 fee is not established on this record.

System records confirm the platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null (F4) — and the cancellation came at 08:19:30, i.e. after the rider had already twice reported she was at the Victoria St entrance with no car to be seen (F3, F8, F10).

The driver's only asserted justification — "Victoria Street was jammed solid" (F13) — is not borne out by the record: Victoria Street is logged at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) at 08:00–08:30, with no traffic incident near the route and fair weather, 0.0 mm rain (F14, F16, F17).
Because the fee is not established the rider's $6.61 cancellation charge should be refunded in full; the amount is the cancellation fee of $6.61 on record, with no surge applied (F3, F6, F7).

The driver's own 90-day record already shows 2 no-show disputes and 2 upheld (F19), while the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days (F18); that history is offered only as support for routing the case to Ryde's account review, not as proof of this incident.

weaknesses: NS-1(i) is still satisfied on the record: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5), so the rider's advocate can argue the tap was made in bad faith to trigger the fee — even though (ii) and (iii) clearly fail (F1, F2, F5).

The rider genuinely waited at the named entrance and said so twice in chat (F8, F10), and the driver's "please come out" message (F9) told her nothing about his true location 613 m away — the rider will use F9 to show she was misled.

There is no GPS breadcrumb proving WHY the driver stopped at (1.2958, 103.8495) (F2) — no road-closure or incident record supports his "jammed solid" explanation (F13, F16), so the reason for his failure to approach is undetermined, not established in his favour.

points.response: Conceded as far as the mechanical fact: F5 does record a tap at 08:16:00, so I do not allege a fabricated or absent tap. But the tap was pressed 613 m out (F5), so NS-1(i) is at best formally ticked while (ii) and (iii) independently fail — the fee still never becomes established, and the abuse-of-button issue is the location of the tap, not its existence (NS-2).

This point is mine, not the driver's: F5 puts the tap 613 m from the pickup point and F1 puts his closest approach at 612 m, so NS-1(ii) fails; his post-hoc explanation (F13) is a statement that loses to those GPS records.

Agreed and adopted: F5 records 0 s within 200 m after the tap, so the continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point required by NS-1(iii) never occurred; his 6 min 20 s stationarity (F2) happened 613 m away and cannot substitute for it.

No dispute: F4 shows driver_arrived_at is null and F3 shows the cancellation at 08:19:30, after the rider had twice stated she was at the entrance with no car visible (F8, F10). These system records, not the rider's statements, carry the finding.

Adopted: F14 puts Victoria Street at band 3 (20–29 km/h), F16 records no incident near the route and F17 fair weather with 0.0 mm rain, so F13's "jammed solid" is contradicted and explains neither the 613 m stand-off nor the tap.
Adopted in full: because no NS-1 condition is met, NS-2 gives the rider a full refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F3, F6) with no surge (F7), issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.

Adopted on account review: the driver tapped "I'm Here" 613 m from the pickup point (F5) and has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F19), while the rider has a clean 90-day record and a 4.9 rating (F18) — profile facts only support the additional flag, they do not decide the case.
Conceded: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null, F4), so the only arrival evidence is the driver's own 08:16:00 tap (F5).
Conceded: the GPS record shows the closest approach was 612 m at 08:15:30 and he never entered 200 m (F1), so NS-1(ii) is not met.
Conceded: the tap was made 613 m from the pickup point (F5), outside any reading of "at the pick-up location", so NS-1(ii) fails.
Conceded: he spent 0 s within 200 m after the tap (F5), so the continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point required by NS-1(iii) never occurred.

Conceded: the stationary period 08:13:10–08:19:30 at 613 m from the pickup point (F2) followed by cancellation at 08:19:30 (F3) is waiting away from the pickup point, which is not waiting for the rider under NS-1(iii).

Conceded: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road at band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incident near the route and fair weather (F14, F15, F16, F17) do not explain a 613 m stand-off, so the driver's "jammed solid" explanation in F13 carries no weight.

Conceded: the chat shows the rider reporting she was at the Victoria St entrance (F8, F10), the driver replying "I'm here already" from 613 m away (F9, F5), then cancelling (F11) — the no-show finding rests on the driver's word alone, which NS-1 does not accept.

Conceded as to the fee: NS-1(ii) and (iii) fail, so under NS-2 the $6.61 on record (F6) is refunded in full (no surge, F7). The flag_account rider C8 also seeks is supported only by profile history (F18, F19), which cannot decide this trip and which NS-2 attaches only where the marked-arrival location requirement was breached; I do not contest it here, since the GPS breach is on the record (F1, F5).
